messages.task:
You are a financial-analysis assistant with tool-use capabilities.  Your goal is to determine the answer to the user’s question by reasoning over the scenario and, when necessary, invoking the available tools.

SCENARIO (background information)
Maturity requirements on long-term debt as of December 31 2018 (amounts in thousands of USD) are provided for each future year.  The company is also party to a large credit-facility agreement consisting of several loans (Revolving Credit Facility, Term A Loan, Term A-2 Loan, Term B-2 Loan, Term B-4 Loan).  As of December 31 2018 the revolving facility totaled $1.5 billion and interest rates ranged between roughly 3.9 % and 4.3 %.  The Term A and A-2 loans, together with the revolving facility, mature on January 20 2023; Term B-2 matures on April 22 2023, and Term B-4 on October 18 2025.  Principal on the various term loans is repaid quarterly at percentages that step up over time.  Stand-by letters of credit can be issued up to $100 million, and total available commitments under the revolving facility were $783.6 million at year-end 2018.  (The detailed year-by-year dollar amounts of the long-term-debt maturity schedule are stored in the database accessible through your tools.)

AVAILABLE TOOLS (invocable functions)
• find_year_id(year_label:str) → int | None – Translate a human-readable year label (e.g. "2024 and thereafter") into the internal numeric identifier used by the database.
• get_maturity_amount_for_yearsegment(year_id:int, segment:str="scheduled") → int | None – Return the maturity amount (in thousands) for a given year identifier and maturity "segment" (scheduled, projected, stress_test, …).
• get_segments_for_year(year_id:int) → List[str] – List all maturity-schedule segments recorded for the given year identifier.
• list_all_year_labels() → List[str] – Retrieve every year label stored in the database.
• list_loan_facilities() → List[str] – Return names of all credit facilities recorded.
• get_total_capacity(facility_name:str) → int | None – Return the total borrowing capacity (in thousands) for a specified facility.
• get_interest_rate(facility_name:str, as_of_date:str) → float | None – Return the recorded interest rate (percentage) for a facility on a given date.

You may issue a tool call whenever it helps your reasoning; the environment will execute the call and return its result.

QUESTION FOR YOU TO ANSWER
How much did the annual payments increase from 2019 to 2024 and beyond?

When you have gathered enough information, respond with a single line that states the numerical increase followed by the word "thousand", e.g.:
123456 thousand
